extracted.intended_audience: rulers, statesmen, jurists, and readers of political philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of principles governing sovereign powers, the nature and practice of counsel, money, colonies, and civil law in a commonwealth. Provides normative rules about who makes laws, how counsel should be given and received, and what counts as law.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Places And Matter Of Traffique Depend On The Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: As the Distribution of Lands at home; so also to assigne in what places, and for what commodities, the Subject shall traffique abroad, belongeth to the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If private persons had discretion, some would furnish enemies or import things noxious or unprofitable; therefore the Common-wealth (the Sovereign) ought to approve or disapprove both the places and matter of foreign traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Laws Of Transferring Property Belong To The Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: It belongeth to the Common-wealth (that is to say, to the Soveraign,) to appoint in what manner, all kinds of contract between Subjects (as buying, selling, exchanging, borrowing, lending, letting, and taking to hire,) are to be made; and by what words, and signes they shall be understood for valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign prescribes form, words and signs that constitute valid contracts and transfers of property; regulation of exchange/transfer is necessary because all arts and commodities are necessary to men's welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money Is The Blood Of A Commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: By Concoction... I understand the reducing of all commodities... to some thing of equal value, and withall so portably, as not to hinder the motion of men... And this is nothing else but Gold, and Silver, and Mony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gold and silver serve as convenient measures of value between nations; money coined by the sovereign measures value within a commonwealth. Precious metals are privileged because their value cannot be easily altered by one or a few commonwealths; base money (value from stamp) is local and subject to legal change and debasement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduits And Ways Of Money To Public Use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conduits, and Wayes by which it is conveyed to the Publique use, are of two sorts; One, that Conveyeth it to the Publique Coffers; The Other, that Issueth the same out againe for publique payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors, receivers, and treasurers bring money into public coffers; treasurers and payment officers issue funds out again. The public financial system is analogised to bodily circulation (veins, heart, arteries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonies Are Children Of A Commonwealth; Their Rights Depend On The Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The Procreation, or Children of a Common-wealth, are those we call Plantations, or Colonies... when a Colony is setled, they are either a Common-wealth of themselves... or else they remain united to their Metropolis... So that the Right of Colonies (saving Honour, and League with their Metropolis,) dependeth wholly on their Licence, or Letters, by which their Soveraign authorised them to Plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies may become independent commonwealths or provinces of the mother commonwealth; their legal status and rights depend on the license/letters granted by the sovereign who sent them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command Versus Counsell — Nature of Command
rubrics_metrics.description: COMMAND is, where a man saith, 'Doe this,' or 'Doe this not,' without expecting other reason than the Will of him that sayes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Command derives authority from the will of the commander and is directed to the commander's own benefit; commands may create obligations (e.g., where one has covenanted to obey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Command Versus Counsell — Nature of Counsell
rubrics_metrics.description: COUNSELL, is where a man saith, 'Doe' or 'Doe not this,' and deduceth his own reasons from the benefit that arriveth by it to him to whom he sayes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel is aimed at the good of the advisee, not the adviser; one cannot claim a right to be of another's counsel; a person who asks counsel cannot justly punish the counsellor for honest advice; counsel does not impose obligation unless contracted into law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhortation And Dehortation Are Vehemently-Pressed Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: EXHORTATION, and DEHORTATION, is Counsell, accompanied with signes in him that giveth it, of vehement desire to have it followed... Counsell Vehemently Pressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhortation uses passions, similitudes, metaphors and oratory to persuade, and is typically directed at multitudes; because it serves the speaker's interests, it tends to be corrupting when given as counsel. When used by rightful commanders (e.g., a father or military leader) exhortation may be lawful and necessary, but then it functions as command.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Good Counsellor's Ends Must Align With The Counseled
rubrics_metrics.description: The first condition of a good Counsellour, That His Ends, And Interest, Be Not Inconsistent With The Ends And Interest Of Him He Counselleth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsellors whose private ends conflict with the commonwealth's are untrustworthy; a counsellor's integrity requires that his interests not oppose those of whom he advises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel Should Present Firm Reasoning, Clear Language, And Brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: He ought to propound his advise, in such forme of speech, as may make the truth most evidently appear; that is to say, with as firme ratiocination, as significant and proper language, and as briefly, as the evidence will permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rash or unevident inferences (mere examples or authority), obscure/confused/ambiguous expressions, and metaphoric speech that stirs passions—these are repugnant to the office of a counsellor because they can deceive or lead the sovereign toward other ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise And Experience Are Required For Good Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: No Man Is Presumed To Be A Good Counsellour, But In Such Businesse, As He Hath Not Onely Been Much Versed In, But Hath Also Much Meditated On, And Considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counseling depends on experience and long study; one is only a competent counsellor in matters one has studied and observed; complex administration requires knowledge of human disposition, law, justice, honour, and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsellors For Foreign Affairs Must Have Proper Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: To be able to give Counsell to a Common-wealth, in a businesse that hath reference to another Common-wealth, It Is Necessary To Be Acquainted With The Intelligences, And Letters That Come From Thence, And With All The Records Of Treaties, And Other Transactions Of State Between Them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel on interstate matters requires access to foreign intelligence, correspondence, and treaty records; only those the representative deems fit can render good counsel in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Individual Hearing Over Large Assemblies For Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Supposing the number of Counsellors equall, a man is better Counselled by hearing them apart, then in an Assembly...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing counsellors separately preserves independent opinions, permits examination and objection, avoids eloquence-driven conformity, and prevents the amplification of passions. Large assemblies risk faction, ambition for applause, and delay; secret small councils or a few trusted advisers are preferable for serious or secret deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Legislator Is The Sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislator in all Common-wealths, is only the Soveraign, be he one Man... or one Assembly of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law is the command of the commonwealth, and because the commonwealth acts by its representative (the sovereign), the sovereign is the sole maker of law; only the sovereign can abrogate a law.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sovereign Is Not Subject To Civil Laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soveraign of a Common-wealth... is not subject to the Civill Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the sovereign has the power to make and repeal laws, he can free himself from them by changing them; being able to release oneself implies freedom; a person cannot be bound to oneself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom Or Long Use Does Not Make A Law Without Sovereign Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: When long Use obtaineth the authority of a Law, it is not the Length of Time that maketh the Authority, but the Will of the Soveraign signified by his silence...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive force of custom depends on the sovereign's seeming consent (silence) rather than mere passage of time; questions grounded on past laws are judged by equity if the sovereign's present will differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Law Of Nature And Civil Law Contain Each Other
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law of Nature, and the Civill Law, contain each other, and are of equall extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural virtues (equity, justice, gratitude) become civil law when enforced by the sovereign; reciprocally, civil obedience is part of natural law because subjects covenant to obey; the distinction is between written (civil) and unwritten (natural) parts of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provincial Customs Are Law Because Of The Present Sovereign's Constitutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Soveraign of one Common-wealth, subdue a people... and afterwards govern them by the same Lawes, by which they were governed before; yet those Lawes are the Civill Lawes of the Victor... the Legislator is he, not by whose authority the Lawes were first made, but by whose authority they now continue to be Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity of provincial laws within a dominion exists because the present sovereign has kept or adopted them; unwritten local laws that are generally observed without injustice are laws of nature rather than mere prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Is The Command Of The Commonwealth — Its Reason Is The Commonwealth's Reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing then all Lawes... have their Authority, and force, from the Will of the Common-wealth... it is not that Juris Prudentia, or wisedome of subordinate Judges; but the Reason of this our Artificiall Man the Common-wealth, and his Command, that maketh Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law's legitimacy rests on the sovereign's will/reason, not private reasoning of judges; subordinate judges should align sentences with the sovereign's intention; differing private reasons among judges would create contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Made But Not Made Known Is No Law
rubrics_metrics.description: From this, that the Law is a Command... we may understand, that the Command of the Common-wealth, is Law onely to those, that have means to take notice of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws must be declared by word, writing, or other sufficient sign to bind subjects; those who, through no fault of theirs, lack means to know a law are excused; over natural fools, children, or mad-men there is no law in the proper sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten Laws That Bind Universally Are Laws Of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be a Law that obliges all the Subjects without exception, and is not written, nor otherwise published... it is a Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws knowable by reason and agreeable to all (e.g., Do not that to another which thou thinkest unreasonable...) do not require proclamation. Similarly, unwritten instructions applicable to specific officers (judges, ambassadors) are to be taken from reason and fidelity when written instruction is absent.
